executiveView.title: Automated AST Analysis Platform & Web Portal
executiveView.summary: An enterprise monorepo featuring an automated AST-driven code analysis CLI tool (handoff-cli) and a fullstack Next.js web application (handoff-web). The CLI uses Tree-sitter parsers across 10+ languages to extract symbols, sanitizes secrets using entropy analysis, inspects Git history, and synthesizes technical handoff documentation using Google Generative AI. The web platform provides authentication, user onboarding, password recovery workflows, and a modern dashboard UI.
executiveView.businessValue: Accelerates developer onboarding by up to 80% through automated repository reverse-engineering and structural documentation generation. Mitigates compliance risks and data leaks by automatically scanning and redacting high-entropy secrets prior to AI model ingestion.
featuresDelivered: Multi-language AST symbol extraction across TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, C++, C#, Ruby, Rust, and PHP powered by Tree-sitter
High-entropy secret detection and automated source code redaction engine
Git metadata, branch commit history, and diff summary parser using simple-git
Map-reduce domain chunking and report synthesis using Google Generative AI
Content hashing cache engine for incremental parsing performance
Standalone interactive HTML report generation with embedded Mermaid.js architecture diagrams
Fullstack web application built with Next.js App Router, Tailwind CSS v4, and React 19
Complete user authentication lifecycle including registration, verification, login, password recovery, and rate-limited API routes

steps.action: Operator executes `handoff` CLI command in target repository.
ASTExtractor scans repository files, builds directory tree, and parses AST symbols.
Sanitizer identifies and redacts high-entropy secrets and sensitive strings.
Map-reduce engine chunks sanitized code and requests AI summary from Google Generative AI.
User accesses `/register` page in handoff-web UI.
User submits credentials which post to `/api/register` endpoint.
System creates user record and dispatches verification email via `/api/resend`.
User clicks link redirecting to `/verify` which posts token to `/api/verify`.
User gets redirected to `/dash` dashboard upon successful token validation.

developerRunbook.architectureOverview: This repository is structured as an enterprise monorepo containing two main projects: `handoff-cli` (an AST analysis engine) and `handoff-web` (a Next.js 16 web portal). The CLI module leverages native Tree-sitter bindings for language parsing, `simple-git` for Git commit extraction, and `@google/generative-ai` for map-reduce document synthesis. The Web application utilizes Next.js App Router with React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, `@supabase/ssr` for authentication state management, and `@upstash/ratelimit` for API rate-limiting enforcement.

coreModules.purpose: Main CLI execution engine managing input parsing, monorepo context checks, and pipeline control.
Tree-sitter AST parser that analyzes multi-language source code files and builds abstract syntax structures.
Entropy detection engine that redacts sensitive keys and filters excluded file paths prior to LLM processing.
Map-reduce summarization pipeline communicating with Google Generative AI SDK.
Local content hashing and disk/memory caching service for incremental code analysis.
Git metadata processing utility extracting commit history, branch info, and repository diffs.
Renders standalone, interactive HTML reports with embedded Mermaid.js diagrams.
Structural report verification engine ensuring compliance against JSON schemas.
Next.js HTTP middleware enforcing route protection and access control.

setupInstructions: Clone repository and ensure Node.js (>=20.x) and pnpm/npm are installed.
Install dependencies at repository root: `npm install`.
Navigate to `handoff-cli/` and copy sample env: `cp .env.example .env` (set `GEMINI_API_KEY`).
Build and test handoff CLI: `cd handoff-cli && npm run build && npm start`.
Navigate to `handoff-web/` and configure environment variables in `.env.local` for Supabase and Upstash.
Run local web development server: `cd handoff-web && npm run dev`.
Open `http://localhost:3000` to access the web application interface.
